To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SC is a major input structure to the basal ganglia that carries information concerning the onset, location, and significance of biologically relevant events.
the SC sends parallel, functionally segregated signals to all the major input nuclei of the BG.
The superior colliculus provides a robust example of a parallel, closed-loop architecture involving subcortical sensorimotor structures and the basal ganglia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the basal ganglion in the control of movement.
the interactions of the SC with the basal ganglion.
the interactions between the midbrain superior colliculus and the basal ganglia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SC is a major source of afferent information to the basal ganglia and that it provides the basal ganglia system with a rich source of information concerning the occurrence of biologically significant external events.

the superior collicular projections to the basal ganglia are consistent with the loop hypothesis, and provide a good model against which the loop characteristics of other basal ganglia projections can be evaluated.
there are at least three parallel, functionally segregated, re-entrant loops linking the basal ganglia to the SC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SC is a key component of an extended basal ganglia system.
the SC is an important component of the basal ganglion system and that it may provide a key link between the sensory processing and the motor control systems of the brain.
the SC is a key structure for integrating information from the environment and the body with basal ganglia function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the basal ganglia are not only involved in cortical processing, but they also have a role in processing subcortical information.
the SC is a critical component in a closed-loop system that is capable of selecting and reinforcing behaviour.
the basal ganglia may have evolved as part of an extended loop architecture involving the SC.
